<script>
/* Reference behaviour for the component contract in component.md. Rebuild it
   idiomatically in your framework — what must survive the rewrite is the one
   shared surface, the two show paths with their different delays, the four
   dismissals, and aria-describedby living only while the surface is shown. */

const POINTER_DELAY_MS = 350
const VIEWPORT_GAP_PX = 8

/* One surface, authored in the markup so it is visible with scripts off, then
   lifted to the body so it escapes every scroll container and stacking
   context on the page. Moved, never cloned. */
const tip = document.getElementById('ds-tooltip-demo')
tip.classList.remove('demo-parked')
tip.hidden = true
document.body.appendChild(tip)
document.querySelector('.demo-specimen').remove()

const surfacesOut = document.getElementById('demo-surfaces')
const triggersOut = document.getElementById('demo-triggers')
const lastOut = document.getElementById('demo-last')

let timer = null
/* The trigger the delay is counting down for. Without it, crossing from a
   button onto its own glyph re-fires pointerover, restarts the timer, and a
   pointer that keeps moving inside one trigger never reaches 350 ms. */
let pending = null
let owner = null

function esc(text) {
  return text.replace(/[&<>]/g, (char) => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;' })[char])
}

/* Preferred side first — inline-start, so a right-docked pane's tooltip lands
   over the page and not off it. Flip only when that side has no room, then
   clamp vertically so a trigger near an edge cannot push the surface out. */
function place(trigger) {
  const anchor = trigger.getBoundingClientRect()
  const surface = tip.getBoundingClientRect()
  let left = anchor.left - surface.width - VIEWPORT_GAP_PX
  if (left < VIEWPORT_GAP_PX) {
    left = Math.min(anchor.right + VIEWPORT_GAP_PX, window.innerWidth - surface.width - VIEWPORT_GAP_PX)
  }
  const centred = anchor.top + anchor.height / 2 - surface.height / 2
  const top = Math.max(
    VIEWPORT_GAP_PX,
    Math.min(centred, window.innerHeight - surface.height - VIEWPORT_GAP_PX),
  )
  tip.style.setProperty('--ds-tooltip-left', Math.round(left) + 'px')
  tip.style.setProperty('--ds-tooltip-top', Math.round(top) + 'px')
}

function show(trigger, source) {
  const title = trigger.dataset.tipTitle
  tip.innerHTML =
    (title ? '<span class="ds-tooltip-title">' + esc(title) + '</span>' : '') + esc(trigger.dataset.tip)
  /* The surface sits on the body, outside the container it describes. Mirror
     that container's forced mode so it is not lit by the page's mode instead. */
  const scope = trigger.closest('[data-mode]')
  if (scope) tip.setAttribute('data-mode', scope.dataset.mode)
  else tip.removeAttribute('data-mode')
  tip.hidden = false
  place(trigger)
  trigger.setAttribute('aria-describedby', tip.id)
  pending = null
  owner = trigger
  lastOut.textContent = source
}

function hide() {
  window.clearTimeout(timer)
  timer = null
  pending = null
  if (owner) {
    owner.removeAttribute('aria-describedby')
    owner = null
  }
  tip.hidden = true
}

document.addEventListener('pointerover', (event) => {
  const trigger = event.target.closest('[data-tip]')
  if (!trigger) {
    if (owner || timer) hide()
    return
  }
  if (trigger === owner || trigger === pending) return
  hide()
  pending = trigger
  timer = window.setTimeout(() => show(trigger, 'pointer, after ' + POINTER_DELAY_MS + ' ms'), POINTER_DELAY_MS)
})

/* Keyboard focus shows at once: the delay exists to keep a pointer crossing
   the list from firing every row, and a keyboard has no such crossing.
   :focus-visible, not :focus — clicking a control must not draw a tooltip on
   top of the thing that was just clicked. */
document.addEventListener('focusin', (event) => {
  const trigger = event.target.closest('[data-tip]')
  if (trigger && trigger.matches(':focus-visible')) show(trigger, 'keyboard, immediately')
  else hide()
})

document.addEventListener('focusout', hide)
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', hide)
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key === 'Escape') hide()
})
/* Capture, so a scroll inside any nested container dismisses too — otherwise
   the surface stays put while the row it describes slides away. */
window.addEventListener('scroll', hide, true)
window.addEventListener('resize', hide)

surfacesOut.textContent = String(document.querySelectorAll('.ds-tooltip').length)
triggersOut.textContent = String(document.querySelectorAll('[data-tip]').length)
</script>
</body>
</html>

Truncated text

Drag a pane's corner to resize it. Clipped now: — Tooltips attach only to those.

Light — single-line rows: the short title never gets a tooltip; the long ones do, until the pane grows past them.

Multiline — the blurb clamps to two lines and earns its tooltip by height, only when a line is actually hidden.

Refuses sample data, stubbed transports, and disconnected UI state as completion evidence, and walks the reviewer through what actually ran.

Dark — same measurement, same one tooltip surface.

Text that ellipsis-truncates in a constrained box and restates itself in a tooltip only when it is actually cut off. Extracted from the shipped TruncatedText primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/TruncatedText.tsx).

This component is the enforcement of the tooltip's restate-only-when-cut-off rule (see components/tooltip): a tooltip repeating a title the person can already read is noise, so the tooltip attaches only while the text overflows. It is the default treatment for every title, label, and path in a width-constrained slot — panel-header titles, board-lane labels, row titles.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Text | .ds-truncated-text | yes — applied to the real element: a <span>, <p>, or the actual <h2> |

One part. The tooltip, when earned, is the system tooltip component — this entry adds no surface of its own.

Variants

  • Default — single line: nowrap, hidden overflow, ellipsis. Overflow is measured by width (scrollWidth > clientWidth).
  • --multiline — a line clamp for blurbs and descriptions: --ds-truncated-lines (default 2) sets the count, and overflow is measured by height (scrollHeight > clientHeight) so the tooltip appears only when the clamp actually hides a line.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Fits | Plain text. No tooltip, no aria-describedby, no cursor change | | Clipped | Ellipsis, and the tooltip contract attaches: shown on hover after the pointer delay, immediately on :focus-visible of the trigger |

The two states are visually identical up to the ellipsis — being clipped is not an error and gets no tint or underline.

Usage

Measure, never assume. Attach the tooltip from a real overflow measurement, with a +1px tolerance so sub-pixel rounding cannot report a false overflow. Re-measure when the text changes and when anything resizes — the element, its container, or the window. A truncation state computed once at mount is wrong after the first pane resize.

The ellipsis needs a shrinkable box. In flex layouts the element (or its wrapper) needs min-width: 0 — without it the flex item refuses to shrink and the ellipsis never triggers. This is the single most common way the component silently fails.

Keep the element's semantics. Apply the class to the real element — the <h2> stays an <h2>, and an id referenced by aria-labelledby elsewhere stays on it. Truncation is a paint decision and must not restructure the document.

The tooltip restates, it does not add. The tooltip content is the full text, verbatim. A *description* the row has no room for is a different job with a different rule: it must stay reachable without hovering (detail pane, menu), per the tooltip contract.

Clamp lines, not height. The multiline variant clamps to a line count. Cutting at a pixel height slices a line in half and hides whether anything was hidden.

Accessibility

  • The full text stays in the document — truncation is visual (text-overflow), so screen readers read the whole value with no tooltip needed. The tooltip serves sighted pointer and keyboard users.
  • When the tooltip is attached, the trigger follows the tooltip contract: aria-describedby only while shown, Escape and scroll dismiss.
  • A clipped value on a non-interactive, non-focusable element is invisible to keyboard users — the tooltip's hover path is the only path. Fine for a value that also lives in the detail pane; otherwise put the truncated text on or inside a focusable element.
  • Never swap the full text into the accessible name conditionally — the name is always the full text, clipped or not.

Known drift

  • The shipped Tooltip.tsx that TruncatedText.tsx attaches mounts one tooltip instance per trigger, where the tooltip spec's contract is one surface per document repositioned per trigger. The drift belongs to the tooltip primitive, not to the measurement contract here. Unfiled.
components/truncated-text/component.css
/* Truncated text — ellipsis truncation that earns a tooltip only when the
 * text is actually cut off. Extracted from the shipped TruncatedText
 * primitive (src/renderer/src/components/ui/TruncatedText.tsx).
 *
 * Family contract: this is the enforcement half of the tooltip's
 * restate-only-when-cut-off rule. The class paints the clipping; the
 * consumer's script measures real overflow (scrollWidth/scrollHeight, +1px
 * rounding tolerance) and attaches the system tooltip only while clipped.
 * No tint, no underline: being clipped is not an error. */

/* Single line. min-width: 0 is load-bearing in flex layouts — without it
 * the flex item refuses to shrink and the ellipsis never triggers, which is
 * the single most common way this component silently fails. */
.ds-truncated-text {
  display: block;
  min-width: 0;
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

/* Multi-line: clamp to a LINE COUNT, never a pixel height — a height cut
 * slices a line in half and hides whether anything was hidden. Overflow is
 * measured by height in this variant, so the tooltip appears only when the
 * clamp actually hides a line. */
.ds-truncated-text--multiline {
  display: -webkit-box;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  -webkit-line-clamp: var(--ds-truncated-lines, 2);
  line-clamp: var(--ds-truncated-lines, 2);
  white-space: normal;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

<script>
/* Reference behaviour for the contract in component.md: measure real
   overflow with a +1px rounding tolerance, re-measure on resize, and attach
   the ONE shared tooltip surface only while clipped. Rebuild idiomatically
   in your framework — what must survive is the measurement (width for
   single-line, height for multiline), the re-check on every resize, and a
   tooltip that never appears over text the person can already read. */

const tip = document.createElement('div')
tip.className = 'ds-tooltip'
tip.id = 'ds-truncated-tip'
tip.setAttribute('role', 'tooltip')
tip.hidden = true
document.body.appendChild(tip)

const clippedOut = document.getElementById('demo-clipped')
const targets = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-demo-truncated]'))
let owner = null
let timer = null

function isClipped(el) {
  /* +1 guards against sub-pixel rounding reporting a false overflow. */
  return el.hasAttribute('data-demo-multiline')
    ? el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1
    : el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1
}

function measureAll() {
  let clipped = 0
  targets.forEach((el) => {
    const cut = isClipped(el)
    if (cut) clipped += 1
    else if (owner === el) hide()
    el.toggleAttribute('data-clipped', cut)
  })
  clippedOut.textContent = String(clipped)
}

function show(el) {
  tip.textContent = el.textContent.trim()
  const scope = el.closest('[data-mode]')
  if (scope) tip.setAttribute('data-mode', scope.dataset.mode)
  else tip.removeAttribute('data-mode')
  tip.hidden = false
  const anchor = el.getBoundingClientRect()
  const surface = tip.getBoundingClientRect()
  const top = Math.max(8, anchor.top - surface.height - 8)
  const left = Math.max(8, Math.min(anchor.left, window.innerWidth - surface.width - 8))
  tip.style.setProperty('--ds-tooltip-top', Math.round(top) + 'px')
  tip.style.setProperty('--ds-tooltip-left', Math.round(left) + 'px')
  const trigger = el.closest('button, [tabindex]') ?? el
  trigger.setAttribute('aria-describedby', tip.id)
  owner = el
}

function hide() {
  window.clearTimeout(timer)
  timer = null
  if (owner) {
    const trigger = owner.closest('button, [tabindex]') ?? owner
    trigger.removeAttribute('aria-describedby')
    owner = null
  }
  tip.hidden = true
}

document.addEventListener('pointerover', (event) => {
  const el = event.target.closest('[data-demo-truncated]')
  if (!el || !el.hasAttribute('data-clipped')) {
    if (owner || timer) hide()
    return
  }
  if (el === owner) return
  hide()
  timer = window.setTimeout(() => show(el), 350)
})

document.addEventListener('focusin', (event) => {
  const el =
    event.target.closest('[data-demo-truncated]') ??
    event.target.querySelector?.('[data-demo-truncated]')
  if (el && el.hasAttribute('data-clipped') && event.target.matches(':focus-visible')) show(el)
  else hide()
})

document.addEventListener('focusout', hide)
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key === 'Escape') hide()
})
window.addEventListener('scroll', hide, true)

const observer = new ResizeObserver(measureAll)
targets.forEach((el) => {
  observer.observe(el)
  const pane = el.closest('.demo-pane')
  if (pane) observer.observe(pane)
})
window.addEventListener('resize', measureAll)
measureAll()
</script>
</body>
</html>

Wizard progress

Dashes — short flow, position is the whole message

Labeled — past four steps, people need to know which stations they passed

Roster Review

Where you are in a flow that has a known number of steps, and — once a step is behind you — a way back to it.

Use it only when the total is known and fixed. A flow whose length depends on what the person picks needs a different affordance: a count that changes as you go is worse than no count, because it removes the one thing this component is for. For an indeterminate wait use [liveness](../liveness/component.md); for navigation between peers use [tabs](../tabs/component.md).

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Strip | .ds-wizard | yes — role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max | | Step | .ds-wizard-step | yes — one per step, in order | | Jump control | .ds-wizard-jump | no — only over already-completed steps | | Step label | .ds-wizard-label | labeled variant only |

The progressbar itself is never interactive. Where back-jumping is offered, the controls are a sibling group layered over the strip — a role="progressbar" that is also a button is two contracts on one element, and screen readers announce the wrong one.

Variants

  • Dashes (default) — anonymous hairline segments. Right when the steps have no names worth reading, or the flow is short enough that position is the whole message.
  • Labeled — each step's name inline, done steps ticked, the current one marked. Right past about four steps, where a count stops being orientation and people need to know *which* stations they have passed. Requires step names; without them it is dashes.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Done | filled in accent.primary; ticked in the labeled variant | | Current | filled, and the only step carrying aria-current="step" | | Upcoming | border.default hairline, unfilled, inert | | Jumpable | a done step that is also focusable and activates the back-jump |

Done and current are separable. By default every step before the active one counts as done, which is what a simple wizard wants. A flow whose active step can itself still be working passes the completed count explicitly, so the current step reads as "in progress" rather than "finished" — the difference between "you are on step 3" and "you have finished 3".

Usage

  • Back, never forward. Completed steps are reachable; upcoming ones are not. A wizard exists because the order matters, and a jump-ahead control quietly says it does not.
  • One strip per flow, at the top of the surface it describes.
  • Do not animate the fill between steps. Movement here would mean "alive right now", which is not what a step change is.
  • Never the only statement of where you are. The surface should also say it in words — a heading naming the current step — because a person returning to a half-finished flow reads the heading, not the dashes.

Accessibility

  • The strip is role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, and an accessible name that reads "Step 3 of 6" — with the current step's own name appended when there is one.
  • The current step carries aria-current="step".
  • Jump controls are real buttons with their own names ("Back to Project"), not bare dashes: "button" repeated six times orients nobody.
  • Upcoming steps are not focusable and are not announced as available.
  • State is never carried by fill colour alone — done steps tick in the labeled variant, and the accessible name always carries the position.

Shipped implementation

src/renderer/src/components/ui/WizardProgress.tsx.

components/wizard-progress/component.css
/* Wizard progress — position in a flow of known length.
 *
 * The strip is a status indicator and nothing else. Where back-jumping is
 * offered the controls are a SIBLING group layered over it, because a
 * role="progressbar" that is also a button carries two contracts on one element
 * and assistive tech announces the wrong one. */

.ds-wizard {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
}

.ds-wizard-step {
  height: 2px;
  min-width: 24px;
  flex: 1 1 auto;
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-pill);
  background: var(--sem-color-border-default);
}

.ds-wizard-step[data-state='done'],
.ds-wizard-step[data-state='current'] {
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
}

/* Current is distinguished from done by weight rather than by hue: the accent
 * already means "progressed", and a second accent would need a second meaning. */
.ds-wizard-step[data-state='current'] {
  height: 3px;
}

/* ── labeled variant ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

.ds-wizard--labeled {
  gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
}

.ds-wizard--labeled .ds-wizard-step {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  height: auto;
  min-width: 0;
  flex: 0 1 auto;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: none;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
}

.ds-wizard--labeled .ds-wizard-step[data-state='done'] {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

.ds-wizard--labeled .ds-wizard-step[data-state='current'] {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
}

.ds-wizard-glyph {
  width: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  height: var(--sem-icon-size-xs);
  flex: none;
}

/* ── back-jump controls ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Back, never forward: only a completed step gets one of these. */
.ds-wizard-jump {
  border: 0;
  padding: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: inherit;
  font: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.ds-wizard-jump:focus-visible {
  outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
}

Patterns

Context rail

Context rail

Drilling into a surface replaces the rail. It never mounts a second column of navigation beside the first. One rail, in one column, at one width — and one way out, a chevron leading the surface's bar, next to the name of the thing it leaves.

The rule: one rail, ever

Model pickers

Content starts three columns in. Each one is a list of things to choose, so nothing says which choice the screen is actually about.

Three navigation columns before the first word of content. A surface that seems to need two levels of rail folds the outer level into a group of the one rail, as above — never into a column of its own.

Anatomy

  • Brand row. Fixed above the rail. Outside the swap.
  • Create + narrow. The surface's New … row and its search/filter lead the rail and stay pinned while the list scrolls — the same anatomy on every surface, so there is one place to look.
  • Groups. One list, or several under quiet headings. A heading earns its place only by separating one group from another: over a lone list, or over a list whose search field already names it, it is the same word said twice.
  • Back. A chevron leading the surface's bar, immediately before the surface's name. It restores the rail the surface replaced, and Escape does the same. Still one affordance and one answer — the rail carries none.
    It was a rail row pinned to the column's bottom, and that is the one thing this pattern got wrong. Below a scrollport is the last place the eye goes and the furthest point from the title of the thing being left, so the most-used control on the surface sat where it cost the most to reach. Attaching it to the name reads as "leave this" rather than "go back", which also keeps it distinct from the window's own history back/forward pair elsewhere in the chrome.

The alignment grid

A rail does not get a column to itself — it replaces one, and several rails take turns in the same physical column. So the grid below is not this pattern's house style; it is the contract that lets one rail follow another, and follow the app sidebar it displaces, without the text edge moving. Ruled 2026-08-05 (MC-2101) after all three candidate grids were measured and none of them was being met.

A door rail is a composition: this pattern's column (pinned head, Back row, the swap) carrying list-surface's two-line row. That is why neither pattern alone described the shipped rails, and why the reconciled numbers live here rather than in either one.

  • Title x-offset: 36px. The number everything else serves. It is 4 + 8 + 16 + 8 — scrollport inset, row padding, leading icon slot, gap — and it is where the app sidebar's own workspace rows put their text, so drilling in does not re-flow the column.
  • Scrollport inset space.2xs (4px), matching list-surface's .rail-rows. Not 6px, and not the 10px that shipped: no pattern has ever specified 10px anywhere.
  • Head inset space.sm (8px), matching list-surface's .rail-head. Wider than the scrollport on purpose — full-width controls against inset row fills.
  • Row padding space.2xs / space.sm, gap space.sm — .cr-row, unchanged.
  • Leading icon slot icon.size.sm (16px), fixed and reserved by the rail, never sized by the surface filling it. A surface may render a smaller mark inside it; it may not change the box. This is the whole of MC-2098 and the only reason 36px is stable.
  • Row type: title font.size.body (13px), state line font.size.meta (12px) — list-surface's .rail-row. The shipped rails ran one step smaller on both.
  • Group heading inset 8px, aligned to the row's fill inner edge rather than to its title.
  • Back chevron: a size.control.xs box on the bar's leading edge — .cr-back, icon-only, no label. In a bar that is indented to align its title with the canvas below it, the chevron takes that line and the title follows: the box hangs back by half a step so the glyph, not the button's edge, sits on the grid. Align the box instead and the indent reads as 8px too deep.
  • The empty-filter notice belongs to the rail, rendered inside the scrollport under the head at the row inset. As a sibling of a flex: 1 rail it is pushed to the bottom of the column when the list is empty — furthest from the search field that emptied it.

Measured, not assumed: the app sidebar's own comment claimed a 36px text column for all four of its row families, but its top-nav rows compute to 40px and its section headers to 38px — the comment was written against a 12px icon that shipped at 16px. 36px is what its workspace rows and fold rows actually use, and those are the rows a door rail replaces.

Selection in a two-level rail

  • The rail keeps one focused selection, at bg.selected: the thing the canvas is showing.
  • A group carrying outer context — which horizon, which project, which run — rests at bg.selected-resting permanently, whether or not the rail holds focus. It answers "where am I?", and it must not compete with "what am I looking at?".
  • Mark the group, never infer it from position: which group is the outer one belongs to the surface.

Motion

  • The incoming rail slides in from its leading edge over motion.duration.normal on motion.ease.standard — opacity and one transform, nothing that reflows.
  • Replacement in the same column at the same width is precisely the change a hard cut reads as a glitch: without the slide, everything in the column changes at once with nothing to say it arrived.
  • Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the treatment drops out entirely. A shortened slide is a stutter.

    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .pat-title {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
  .pat-lede {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xl);
  }
  .pat-heading {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-heading);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: var(--sem-space-3xl) 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .pat-caption {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: var(--sem-space-sm) 0 0;
  }
  .pat-verdict {
    display: inline-block;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-wide);
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xs) var(--sem-space-xs);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .pat-list {
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-lg);
    padding-left: var(--sem-space-xl);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
  }
  .pat-list li {
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
  .pat-list strong {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  }
  code {
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }

  /* ── the app frame the pattern is drawn inside ─────────────────────────── */

  .cr-frame {
    display: flex;
    min-height: 268px;
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-shell);
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  /* The ONE navigation column. Every drilled-in surface renders its rail here,
     at this width — in the product that width is the app sidebar's own,
     user-resizable value, so there is exactly one number for it anywhere. */
  .cr-column {
    position: relative;
    width: 208px;
    flex: none;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  .cr-canvas {
    flex: 1;
    min-width: 0;
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    padding: var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-xl);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  }
  .cr-canvas h3 {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-heading);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-md);
  }
  .cr-field {
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xl);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) 0;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    max-width: 44ch;
  }
  .cr-field span:first-child {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  }

  /* Brand row: the fixed header above the rail. It does NOT participate in the
     swap — the product name is not context, it is the window. */
  .cr-brand {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    padding: var(--sem-space-md) var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-sm);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
  }
  .cr-brand em {
    font-style: normal;
    color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  }

  .cr-rail {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    flex: 1;
    min-height: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  /* 4px horizontal is the canonical scrollport inset — see "The alignment grid"
     below. It is deliberately NARROWER than the head above it (8px): the head
     holds full-width controls, the scrollport holds rows whose hover fill is
     inset from the column edge. */
  .cr-scroll {
    flex: 1;
    min-height: 0;
    overflow-y: auto;
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
  .cr-group {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-3xs);
  }
  .cr-row {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
    width: 100%;
    padding: var(--sem-space-2xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font: inherit;
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    text-align: left;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .cr-row:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
  }
  .cr-row:focus-visible {
    outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
    outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  }
  .cr-row-count {
    margin-left: auto;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
  }
  /* The two selection tiers, straight from patterns/selection.html — a neutral
     fill, never the accent, never an edge bar. */
  .cr-row--selected {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  }
  .cr-row--resting {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected-resting);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  /* An outer-context GROUP rests permanently: it says which container you are
     in, not what you are working on, so it never competes for the one focused
     selection — whether or not the rail holds focus. */
  .cr-group-rows--outer .cr-row--selected {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected-resting);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-regular);
  }
  /* The door's bar: its name, and the one control that leaves it. */
  .cr-bar {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
    flex: none;
    height: 36px;
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-md);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
  }
  .cr-bar-title {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;
    white-space: nowrap;
  }
  /* Back: a chevron leading the door's bar, immediately before the door's name.
     It was a rail row pinned to the column's bottom, and the move is the whole
     of this revision — see the Anatomy note. */
  .cr-back {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    flex: none;
    width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    padding: 0;
    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .cr-back:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .cr-back:focus-visible {
    outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
    outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  }
  /* The canvas and the bar above it are one column beside the rail. */
  .cr-body {
    flex: 1;
    min-width: 0;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
  }
  .cr-glyph {
    width: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
    height: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
    flex: none;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }

  /* ── the swap, driven by a checkbox so the motion is real ───────────────── */

  .cr-toggle {
    position: absolute;
    opacity: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
  }
  .cr-swap {
    display: grid;
    flex: 1;
    min-height: 0;
  }
  .cr-swap > .cr-rail {
    grid-area: 1 / 1;
  }
  .cr-toggle:not(:checked) ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--surface,
  .cr-toggle:checked ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--app {
    visibility: hidden;
  }
  .cr-toggle:not(:checked) ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--app,
  .cr-toggle:checked ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--surface {
    animation: cr-swap-in var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard) both;
  }
  .cr-toggle:focus-visible ~ .cr-swap .cr-swap-trigger {
    outline: var(--sem-focus-ring);
    outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset);
  }
  @keyframes cr-swap-in {
    from {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateX(-10px);
    }
    to {
      opacity: 1;
      transform: none;
    }
  }
  /* The whole treatment drops out rather than shortening: a 40ms slide reads as
     a stutter, and the pattern is legible without it. */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .cr-toggle ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail {
      animation: none;
    }
  }

  /* ── the anti-pattern, drawn only here ─────────────────────────────────── */

  .cr-nested .cr-column {
    border-right: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  }
  .cr-nested .cr-column:nth-of-type(2),
  .cr-nested .cr-column:nth-of-type(3) {
    width: 152px;
  }
  .cr-nested-tag {
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
</style>
</head>
<body>

<div class="pat-stage" data-mode="dark">
  <p class="pat-title">Context rail</p>
  <p class="pat-lede">
    Drilling into a surface <em>replaces</em> the rail. It never mounts a second
    column of navigation beside the first. One rail, in one column, at one width —
    and one way out, a chevron leading the surface's bar, next to the name of the
    thing it leaves.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">The rule: one rail, ever</p>
  <p class="pat-verdict">DO</p>
  <div class="cr-frame">
    <div class="cr-column">
      <!-- The brand row is the window, not context: it sits above the rail and
           stays put through every swap. -->
      <div class="cr-brand">sprint<em>engine</em></div>
      <input class="cr-toggle" type="checkbox" id="cr-drill" />
      <div class="cr-swap">
        <div class="cr-rail cr-rail--app">
          <div class="cr-scroll">
            <label class="cr-row cr-swap-trigger" for="cr-drill">
              <svg class="cr-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M4.8 11a3.2 3.2 0 0 1 6.4 0M2 11h12M8 5.4V3.9" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
              Horizon
            </label>
            <div class="cr-group">Projects</div>
            <div class="cr-group-rows">
              <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">multicode</button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">website</button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">relay</button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="cr-rail cr-rail--surface">
          <div class="cr-scroll">
            <!-- Outer level, folded into a GROUP of this one rail rather than
                 given a column of its own. -->
            <div class="cr-group">Horizons</div>
            <div class="cr-group-rows cr-group-rows--outer">
              <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Q3 platform</button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">Mobile beta</button>
            </div>
            <div class="cr-group">Plan</div>
            <div class="cr-group-rows">
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">Type + icon ramp<span class="cr-row-count">9</span></button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Model pickers<span class="cr-row-count">4</span></button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">Provider rows<span class="cr-row-count">6</span></button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-body">
      <div class="cr-bar">
        <!-- Back leads the door's bar. It is a label here only so the demo's
             checkbox can un-drill; in the product it is a button. -->
        <label class="cr-back" for="cr-drill" aria-label="Back">
          <svg class="cr-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
            <path d="M10 3.5 5.5 8l4.5 4.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
        </label>
        <span class="cr-bar-title">Horizon</span>
      </div>
      <div class="cr-canvas">
        <h3>Model pickers</h3>
        <div class="cr-field"><span>Delivered by</span><span>sprint-1932</span></div>
        <div class="cr-field"><span>Track</span><span>Delivery</span></div>
        <div class="cr-field"><span>Depends on</span><span>Type + icon ramp</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Click <strong>Horizon</strong>, then <strong>Back</strong>. The rail is
    replaced in place and slides in from its leading edge; the brand row above it
    does not move, and the canvas keeps the whole of the rest of the window.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">The failure this prevents</p>
  <p class="pat-verdict">DO NOT</p>
  <div class="cr-frame cr-nested">
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-nested-tag">app rail</div>
      <div class="cr-scroll">
        <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--resting" aria-current="true">multicode</button>
        <button type="button" class="cr-row">website</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-nested-tag">door rail</div>
      <div class="cr-scroll">
        <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--resting" aria-current="true">Q3 platform</button>
        <button type="button" class="cr-row">Mobile beta</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-nested-tag">plan column</div>
      <div class="cr-scroll">
        <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Model pickers</button>
        <button type="button" class="cr-row">Provider rows</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-canvas">
      <h3>Model pickers</h3>
      Content starts three columns in. Each one is a list of things to choose,
      so nothing says which choice the screen is actually about.
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Three navigation columns before the first word of content. A surface that
    seems to need two levels of rail folds the outer level into a group of the one
    rail, as above — never into a column of its own.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">Anatomy</p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li><strong>Brand row.</strong> Fixed above the rail. Outside the swap.</li>
    <li><strong>Create + narrow.</strong> The surface's <code>New …</code> row and
      its search/filter lead the rail and stay pinned while the list scrolls —
      the same anatomy on every surface, so there is one place to look.</li>
    <li><strong>Groups.</strong> One list, or several under quiet headings. A
      heading earns its place only by separating one group from another: over a
      lone list, or over a list whose search field already names it, it is the
      same word said twice.</li>
    <li><strong>Back.</strong> A chevron leading the surface's <em>bar</em>,
      immediately before the surface's name. It restores the rail the surface
      replaced, and <code>Escape</code> does the same. Still one affordance and
      one answer — the rail carries none.
      <br />
      It <em>was</em> a rail row pinned to the column's bottom, and that is the
      one thing this pattern got wrong. Below a scrollport is the last place the
      eye goes and the furthest point from the title of the thing being left, so
      the most-used control on the surface sat where it cost the most to reach.
      Attaching it to the name reads as "leave <em>this</em>" rather than "go
      back", which also keeps it distinct from the window's own history
      back/forward pair elsewhere in the chrome.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="pat-heading">The alignment grid</p>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    A rail does not get a column to itself — it <em>replaces</em> one, and several
    rails take turns in the same physical column. So the grid below is not this
    pattern's house style; it is the contract that lets one rail follow another,
    and follow the app sidebar it displaces, without the text edge moving.
    Ruled 2026-08-05 (MC-2101) after all three candidate grids were measured and
    none of them was being met.
  </p>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    A door rail is a <strong>composition</strong>: this pattern's column (pinned
    head, Back row, the swap) carrying <a href="list-surface.html">list-surface</a>'s
    two-line row. That is why neither pattern alone described the shipped rails,
    and why the reconciled numbers live here rather than in either one.
  </p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li><strong>Title x-offset: 36px.</strong> The number everything else serves.
      It is <code>4 + 8 + 16 + 8</code> — scrollport inset, row padding, leading
      icon slot, gap — and it is where the app sidebar's own workspace rows put
      their text, so drilling in does not re-flow the column.</li>
    <li><strong>Scrollport inset <code>space.2xs</code> (4px)</strong>, matching
      list-surface's <code>.rail-rows</code>. Not 6px, and not the 10px that
      shipped: no pattern has ever specified 10px anywhere.</li>
    <li><strong>Head inset <code>space.sm</code> (8px)</strong>, matching
      list-surface's <code>.rail-head</code>. Wider than the scrollport on
      purpose — full-width controls against inset row fills.</li>
    <li><strong>Row padding <code>space.2xs</code> / <code>space.sm</code>, gap
      <code>space.sm</code></strong> — <code>.cr-row</code>, unchanged.</li>
    <li><strong>Leading icon slot <code>icon.size.sm</code> (16px), fixed and
      reserved by the rail</strong>, never sized by the surface filling it. A
      surface may render a smaller mark inside it; it may not change the box.
      This is the whole of MC-2098 and the only reason 36px is stable.</li>
    <li><strong>Row type: title <code>font.size.body</code> (13px), state line
      <code>font.size.meta</code> (12px)</strong> — list-surface's
      <code>.rail-row</code>. The shipped rails ran one step smaller on both.</li>
    <li><strong>Group heading inset 8px</strong>, aligned to the row's fill inner
      edge rather than to its title.</li>
    <li><strong>Back chevron: a <code>size.control.xs</code> box on the bar's
      leading edge</strong> — <code>.cr-back</code>, icon-only, no label. In a
      bar that is indented to align its title with the canvas below it, the
      chevron takes that line and the title follows: the box hangs back by half a
      step so the <em>glyph</em>, not the button's edge, sits on the grid. Align
      the box instead and the indent reads as 8px too deep.</li>
    <li><strong>The empty-filter notice belongs to the rail</strong>, rendered
      inside the scrollport under the head at the row inset. As a sibling of a
      <code>flex: 1</code> rail it is pushed to the bottom of the column when the
      list is empty — furthest from the search field that emptied it.</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Measured, not assumed: the app sidebar's own comment claimed a 36px text
    column for all four of its row families, but its top-nav rows compute to 40px
    and its section headers to 38px — the comment was written against a 12px icon
    that shipped at 16px. 36px is what its <em>workspace rows</em> and fold rows
    actually use, and those are the rows a door rail replaces.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">Selection in a two-level rail</p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li>The rail keeps <strong>one focused selection</strong>, at
      <code>bg.selected</code>: the thing the canvas is showing.</li>
    <li>A group carrying <strong>outer context</strong> — which horizon, which
      project, which run — rests at <code>bg.selected-resting</code>
      <em>permanently</em>, whether or not the rail holds focus. It answers
      "where am I?", and it must not compete with "what am I looking at?".</li>
    <li>Mark the group, never infer it from position: which group is the outer one
      belongs to the surface.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="pat-heading">Motion</p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li>The incoming rail slides in from its leading edge over
      <code>motion.duration.normal</code> on <code>motion.ease.standard</code> —
      opacity and one transform, nothing that reflows.</li>
    <li>Replacement in the same column at the same width is precisely the change a
      hard cut reads as a glitch: without the slide, everything in the column
      changes at once with nothing to say it arrived.</li>
    <li>Under <code>prefers-reduced-motion: reduce</code> the treatment drops out
      entirely. A shortened slide is a stutter.</li>
  </ul>
</div>

<div class="pat-stage" data-mode="light">
  <p class="pat-title">Context rail — light</p>
  <p class="pat-lede">The same one column, the same two tiers, from the same tokens.</p>
  <div class="cr-frame">
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-brand">sprint<em>engine</em></div>
      <div class="cr-rail">
        <div class="cr-scroll">
          <div class="cr-group">Horizons</div>
          <div class="cr-group-rows cr-group-rows--outer">
            <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Q3 platform</button>
            <button type="button" class="cr-row">Mobile beta</button>
          </div>
          <div class="cr-group">Plan</div>
          <div class="cr-group-rows">
            <button type="button" class="cr-row">Type + icon ramp<span class="cr-row-count">9</span></button>
            <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Model pickers<span class="cr-row-count">4</span></button>
            <button type="button" class="cr-row">Provider rows<span class="cr-row-count">6</span></button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-body">
      <div class="cr-bar">
        <button type="button" class="cr-back" aria-label="Back">
          <svg class="cr-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
            <path d="M10 3.5 5.5 8l4.5 4.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
        </button>
        <span class="cr-bar-title">Horizon</span>
      </div>
      <div class="cr-canvas">
        <h3>Model pickers</h3>
        <div class="cr-field"><span>Delivered by</span><span>sprint-1932</span></div>
        <div class="cr-field"><span>Track</span><span>Delivery</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

</body>
</html>

List surface

List surface

The anatomy every rail, column, and panel whose job is “find a thing in a list” is built from. Create, then search with one filter glyph, then one divider, then the rows. Tokens and components alone never caught the defects this pattern exists to prevent — they are all composition defects.

When this surface is the list inside a rail that replaces a column — a door rail rather than a standalone panel — its row belongs to a shared alignment grid, because several rails take turns in that one column. The row numbers here (.rail-rows 4px, .rail-row 6/8px, title body over meta meta) are the ones that grid adopts; the rest of it — scrollport, leading icon slot, Back row, and the 36px title edge they add up to — is ruled in context-rail under "The alignment grid".

The anatomy

Build to this

Search sprints…
  • design-system-conformance 1 merge left
  • skills-aside 1 merge left
  • site-truth-and-impact landed Jul 29

Project, view, sort and group all live inside the glyph. It carries the accent dot because a lens is applied — collapsing the axes must never collapse the fact that one is narrowing the list. One group, so no heading over it.

Not this

All projects · 49 ⌄
Search sprints…
Recent 49
  • design-system-conformance 1 merge left
  • skills-aside 1 merge left

Three defects, all composition: a second full-width control stacked over the field it narrows; the same choice offered as a Select here and as a menu axis elsewhere; and a “Recent” heading spanning every row, which groups nothing. The divider has also drifted below the group heading, so it no longer means “the list starts here”.

Both modes

In a list-plus-detail layout the whole block above — search, glyph, and the divider under them — is constrained to the list column. Spanning the full width reads as “search this screen” while it only ever filters one column.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>List surface</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../foundations/tokens.css" />
<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
    line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  }
  .pat-stage {
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .pat-title {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
  .pat-lede {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xl);
  }
  .pat-heading {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-heading);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: var(--sem-space-3xl) 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .pat-caption {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: var(--sem-space-sm) 0 0;
  }
  .pat-panes {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr));
    gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
    align-items: start;
  }

  /* ── the anatomy ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .rail {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  /* 1+2+3: create, then search with the glyph, then THE divider. */
  .rail-head {
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  }
  .rail-new {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    width: 100%;
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px dashed var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    font: inherit;
    text-align: left;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .rail-new:hover { background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover); color: var(--sem-color-text-primary); }
  .rail-new:focus-visible { outline: var(--sem-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset); }

  .rail-find { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--sem-space-2xs); }
  .rail-search {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    flex: 1;
    min-width: 0;
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .rail-glyph {
    position: relative;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    flex: none;
    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .rail-glyph:hover { background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover); color: var(--sem-color-text-primary); }
  .rail-glyph:focus-visible { outline: var(--sem-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--sem-focus-ring-offset); }
  /* Collapsing the axes hides them; it must never hide that one is applied. */
  .rail-glyph[data-active="true"] { color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary); }
  .rail-glyph[data-active="true"]::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    right: 0;
    width: 6px;
    height: 6px;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-pill);
    background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  }

  /* 4: the rows. */
  .rail-rows { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: var(--sem-space-2xs); }
  .rail-row {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
    padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  }
  .rail-row[aria-current="true"] { background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected); }
  .rail-row-title { color: var(--sem-color-text-default); }
  .rail-row[aria-current="true"] .rail-row-title { color: var(--sem-color-text-primary); }
  .rail-row-meta { font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta); color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle); }
  /* A heading appears only when there are two groups to tell apart. */
  .rail-group {
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-2xs);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }

  /* the rejected shape, for contrast */
  .rail--wrong .rail-scope {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    width: 100%;
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .rail--wrong .rail-head { border-bottom: 0; }
  .rail--wrong .rail-rows { border-top: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle); }
  .pat-verdict {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-xs);
  }
  .pat-verdict[data-tone="good"] { color: var(--sem-color-status-good); }
  .pat-verdict[data-tone="bad"] { color: var(--sem-color-status-danger); }
</style>
</head>

Selection

Selection

Selection answers “what did I pick?”. Focus answers “where am I typing?”. They are different questions and never share a treatment. Selection is a neutral fill in two tiers — the accent is reserved for the primary action, so a chosen row never outranks the one thing worth clicking.

The rule: one focused selection per surface

DO

Marketplacefocus

Sources

Categories

One pane has focus and shows --selected. The other two show --resting: they remember the choice without competing, so the eye lands on the list the keyboard is driving.

The failure this prevents

DO NOT

Marketplace

Sources

Categories

Three panes shouting at once, each with an accent fill and a left bar. Nothing says which list has focus, three signals carry one state, and the accent no longer means “this is the action”. Selection never uses the accent, and never carries a left bar.

Where a left bar is still correct

Only on a collapsed icon rail, where rows are too narrow for a fill to read. Everywhere else — every content list — selection is a fill.

Selection — light

The same two tiers, from the same tokens.

Marketplacefocus

        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">Skills</span></span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">Modules</span></span>
      </button>
    </div>
    <div class="pat-pane">
      <p class="pat-pane-title"><span>Sources</span></p>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">Multicode</span></span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--selected">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">Matt Pocock</span></span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">browser-act</span></span>
      </button>
    </div>
    <div class="pat-pane">
      <p class="pat-pane-title"><span>Categories</span></p>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row ds-list-row--selected">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">Engineering</span></span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">17</span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">Productivity</span></span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">5</span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
        <span class="ds-list-row-text"><span class="ds-list-row-title">In progress</span></span>
        <span class="ds-list-row-trailing">9</span>
      </button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Three panes shouting at once, each with an accent fill and a left bar.
    Nothing says which list has focus, three signals carry one state, and the
    accent no longer means “this is the action”. Selection never uses the
    accent, and never carries a left bar.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">Where a left bar is still correct</p>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Only on a collapsed icon rail, where rows are too narrow for a fill to
    read. Everywhere else — every content list — selection is a fill.
  </p>
</div>

<div class="pat-stage" data-mode="light">

  <p class="pat-lede">The same two tiers, from the same tokens.</p>
  <div class="pat-panes">

      <button type="button" class="ds-list-row">
